message.content:
Below are two ways you can launch a **Compute Engine** instance that has an **NVIDIA RTX A6000** GPU and runs **Ubuntu 20.04 LTS**.

> ⚠️ **Note**  
> * “EC2” is Amazon‑AWS terminology. In Google Cloud the equivalent service is **Compute Engine**.  
> * The RTX A6000 is available as a **GPU accelerator** (`nvidia-tesla-a6000`).  
> * You must have the **Compute Engine API** enabled and the **GPU license** granted for your project.

---

## 1️⃣  gcloud CLI (recommended)

```bash
# 1. Pick a zone that supports GPUs (e.g., us-central1-b)
ZONE="us-central1-b"

# 2. Create the instance
gcloud compute instances create my-rtx-a6000 \
  --zone=$ZONE \
  --machine-type=n1-standard-8 \          # 8 vCPU, 30 GB RAM (adjust as needed)
  --accelerator=type=nvidia-tesla-a6000,count=1 \
  --image-family=ubuntu-2004-lts \
  --image-project=ubuntu-os-cloud \
  --boot-disk-size=100GB \
  --boot-disk-type=pd-ssd \
  --maintenance-policy=MIGRATE \
  --restart-on-failure \
  --metadata-from-file startup-script=startup.sh   # optional: install drivers, etc.
```

### What the flags mean

| Flag | Purpose |
|------|---------|
| `--machine-type` | CPU/RAM configuration. |
| `--accelerator` | Adds the GPU. |
| `--image-family` & `--image-project` | Pulls the latest Ubuntu 20.04 LTS image. |
| `--boot-disk-size/type` | SSD boot disk. |
| `--maintenance-policy` | Keeps the VM running during maintenance. |
| `--restart-on-failure` | Auto‑restarts if the VM crashes. |

> **Tip** – If you need the NVIDIA driver pre‑installed, add a `startup.sh` script that runs `sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535` (or the latest driver version).

---

## 2️⃣  REST API (JSON payload)

If you prefer to use the raw Compute Engine REST API, here’s a minimal request body:

```json
{
  "name": "my-rtx-a6000",
  "machineType": "zones/us-central1-b/machineTypes/n1-standard-8",
  "disks": [
    {
      "boot": true,
      "autoDelete": true,
      "initializeParams": {
        "sourceImage": "projects/ubuntu-os-cloud/global/images/family/ubuntu-2004-lts",
        "diskSizeGb": 100,
        "diskType": "zones/us-central1-b/diskTypes/pd-ssd"
      }
    }
  ],
  "networkInterfaces": [
    {
      "network": "global/networks/default",
      "accessConfigs": [
        { "type": "ONE_TO_ONE_NAT", "name": "External NAT" }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "accelerators": [
    {
      "acceleratorType": "projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-b/acceleratorTypes/nvidia-tesla-a6000",
      "acceleratorCount": 1
    }
  ],
  "serviceAccounts": [
    {
      "email": "default",
      "scopes": [
        "https://www.googleapis.com/auth/cloud-platform"
      ]
    }
  ],
  "metadata": {
    "items": [
      {
        "key": "startup-script",
        "value": "#!/bin/bash\napt-get update\napt-get install -y nvidia-driver-535"
      }
    ]
  }
}
```

### How to send it

```bash
curl -X POST \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $(gcloud auth print-access-token)" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d @instance.json \
  "https://compute.googleapis.com/compute/v1/projects/my-project/zones/us-central1-b/instances"
```

Replace:

* `my-project` – your GCP project ID.
* `us-central1-b` – a zone that supports GPUs.
* `nvidia-driver-535` – the driver version you want to install (check NVIDIA’s site for the latest).

---

## 3️⃣  Quick sanity check

After launching, verify the GPU is visible:

```bash
gcloud compute ssh my-rtx-a6000 --zone=us-central1-b --command "nvidia-smi"
```

You should see the RTX A6000 listed with its driver version.

---

### Recap

| Step | Command | What it does |
|------|---------|--------------|
| 1 | `gcloud compute instances create …` | Creates the VM with GPU via CLI. |
| 2 | REST JSON payload | Same thing, but via HTTP. |
| 3 | `nvidia-smi` | Confirms the GPU is present. |

Feel free to tweak the machine type, disk size, or add more GPUs if your workload demands it. Happy computing!
